text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three foreign investors - Giro credit, EBRD,IFC - will buy 51 percent or 50 percent plus three shares of Macedonia's biggest bank Stopanska Banka. Giro credit will take over the management of Stopanska banka in the name of the three investors.
- New president of Macedonian constitutional court for the next three years is Milan Netkov.
- Nova Makedonija correspondent from Ohrid Dimitar Pejinevski heavily beaten in Ohrid. The beating is linked to his writing about organised violence in this town.
- Macedonian parliament to vote confidence at noon on Thursday in the newly reshuffled government led by Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski.

- Almost all political parties in Macedonia say the new cabinet will not bring any changes to the country. Macedonia needs new politics not new cabinets that are changed by the same prime minister, they say.

- Six demonstrators taken into police custody following violent demostrations of a few thousand depositors of bankrupt financial institution TAT in Bitola on Tuesday. Houses of Bitola mayor Siljan Micevski and TAT owner Sonja Nikolovska under strong police protection. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
